title: Z² Snaps Philly's Streak by 1.74 While the Horse Gallops Back Into the Title Race
dek: Ghostu-Spider SZN stunned Team Pillbert as a 28% underdog, The Horse is Hea dropped the week's top score on Randy, and the HULK kept winning even as its title odds slipped.
body: The rookie did it again. Zoe's Ghostu-Spider SZN beat Alan's Team Pillbert 87.96 to 86.22, winning as a 28% underdog and ending Philly's five-game win streak by less than two points. She pulled it off with Nico Collins giving her 1.6 points on a 14.01 projection, which means the rest of the web had to do overtime. Earlier this season Z² knocked off Sonny, and now she has beaten both of the teams tied for second place. Her record says 3-4; the list of contenders she's taken down says she belongs.

For Philly, a 1.74-point loss means every dud in the lineup gets a turn at the blame, and Jalen Coker earns the first slot: 1.4 points on a 12.57 projection. Javonte Williams did his part with 21.5, but Justin Jefferson managed 6.4 and Chuba Hubbard 8. DeVonta Smith did not play and was rightly left out of the lineup. Team Pillbert slips to 5-2, its title odds fall from 26% to 17%, and the playoff odds remain a sturdy 93%. Zoey's win nudges her playoff odds to 6%, and she swapped David Montgomery for Blake Corum on the way out the door.

The loudest scoreboard of the week belonged to Sonny. The Horse is Hea crushed Randy's The fumblers 146.72 to 108.52, the top total of week 7, behind Jaxon Smith-Njigba (26.8 on a 16.25 projection), Jameson Williams (23.6 on just 8.95) and Bucky Irving (23.5). The pieces from the Philly trade finally showed up in the lineup too, with Ollie Gordon II scoring 16.8 and George Pickens 13.7. The model loved it: the Horse's title odds jumped from 11% to 28%, second-best in the league. Sonny also rebuilt the stable on the wire, swapping Patrick Mahomes for Lamar Jackson, Bryce Young for C.J. Stroud, Cam Skattebo for Jordan Mason and Terry McLaurin for Will Reichard. He even dropped Emanuel Wilson for Zach Charbonnet, then cut Cam Little to bring Wilson right back.

Randy got a good afternoon from Caleb Williams, 22.12 on a 17.59 projection, but Derrick Henry went for 5.4 on a 17.37 projection, and that's two straight weeks of single digits from the back who is supposed to anchor the roster. Stefon Diggs was on bye. The fumblers have now lost four in a row, sit at 3-4 and have 23% playoff odds. Randy answered with a full purge: Kenny Gainwell, Alec Pierce, Darren Waller, Jordan Addison and the Rams D/ST are gone, and Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas, Cameron Dicker, the Browns D/ST and the Bears D/ST are in. Yes, that's the same Bears defense Sonny released last week. It found its way back to a Chicago home.

Kaushal's Habibsters beat Mekhi's Dawgs 119.84 to 93.58 in a game the model called a pure coin flip. Drake Maye kept rewarding Habib's waiver work with 27.44 points on a 20.59 projection, the second-best individual score of the week. The funny part: Tony Pollard put up 35 points on the Habibsters bench, the biggest benched score in the league, and Habib won by 26 anyway. That's two straight wins, a 3-4 record and fourth place on points, with title odds up from 6% to 14% and playoff odds at 67%. Kaushal kept tinkering, adding Germie Bernard and Tre Tucker while letting go of the Chiefs D/ST and Juwan Johnson.

Kai had his own bench headache, with Tee Higgins scoring 23.8 as a reserve, though that alone wouldn't have closed a 26.26-point gap. Ashton Jeanty gave him 17.6, while Davante Adams did not play. The Dawgs fall to 2-5 with 14% playoff odds, and Mekhi added Aaron Rodgers without dropping anyone, which tells you the waiver king is still shopping. Over at the top, Ramon's No Banner only HULK handled Jordan's Counting or not Counting GV 98 to 60.88 as an 85% favorite. Brucie left Zay Flowers' 23.7 on the bench and didn't need it, and he picked up kicker Brandon Aubrey, the same Aubrey Randy cut last week, in place of Eddy Pineiro.

JMoney's week was a strange one: Joe Burrow scored 28.88 on a 19.31 projection, the best individual game in the league, and the rest of the lineup combined for 32. Isaiah Likely scored 2.2 and Denzel Boston 4.2, and Emeka Egbuka did not play. Jordan swapped Ladd McConkey for J.K. Dobbins, but at 1-6 and 0% playoff odds he is playing for pride now. The HULK, meanwhile, is 6-1 on a three-game streak with 927.4 points for, yet its title odds dropped from 50% to 36%, a sign of how seriously the model takes the Horse's surge.

Week 8 has a headliner: Team Pillbert hosts The Horse is Hea with both teams at 5-2 and second place on the line, and Philly gets a shot at Sonny right after the Horse won the box score on their trade. Habib and Zoe meet as 3-4 teams that both won this week, a real playoff elimination game in disguise. Randy needs to snap a four-game skid against JMoney, which on paper is the friendliest matchup he'll see all year. And the HULK hosts Kai, who knows the wire better than anyone but needs his lineup choices to finally cooperate.

social.author: Ghostu-Spider SZN
social.text: MATCHDAY RESULT: Ghostu-Spider SZN 87.96, Team Pillbert 86.22. 🕷️ A five-game streak caught in the web. 3-4 and Habibsters next. Let's keep spinning.

social.author: Dana Whitfield
social.text: Busy wire: The Horse is Hea made seven moves, including Lamar Jackson for Patrick Mahomes and C.J. Stroud for Bryce Young. The fumblers dropped five players and added five, among them both the Browns and Bears D/ST. No trades this week.

social.author: Sunday Spreadsheet Sam
social.text: The HULK won by 37 and lost 14 points of title odds. The Horse won by 38 and gained 17. Week 8: Horse at Pillbert. The model has picked its sleeper.

social.author: Bench Points Betty
social.text: Week 7 bench report: Tony Pollard 35, Tee Higgins 23.8, Zay Flowers 23.7. Two of the three managers won anyway. Habib, you have to see that 35, right?

social.author: Fumble Faithful Frank
social.text: Caleb gave us 22.12 and Henry gave us 5.4. Four straight losses. Randy cut half the roster and brought the Bears D back. At least the vibes are right. 🐻

social.author: Counting Crew Carla
social.text: Joe Burrow: 28.88, best game in the league. Everyone else: 32 combined. We scored 60.88. I'm not mad, I'm just tired. 🎺

social.author: Gridiron Gary
social.text: Habibsters: two straight wins, title odds from 6% to 14%, and they did it with a 35-point back on the bench. Fourth place belongs to the two-time champ again. Never count out Habib.

trade_watch.take: The flip is on. Gordon (16.8) and Pickens (13.7) gave Sonny 30.5 lineup points in a blowout, while Hubbard managed 8 and Smith did not play as Philly lost by 1.74. A week ago this looked like Alan's trade; now the Horse is the one gaining title odds.
Still Philly's deal, and widening: Javonte Williams scored 21.5 and has 75.5 since the trade, every point in Alan's lineup. Diggs was on bye, so Randy's in-lineup side stays stuck at 6.

Kai's side keeps producing: Jeanty added 17.6, pushing the Dawgs' lineup haul from this deal to 65.6, while Adams did not play. Jefferson scored 6.4 in a one-point-ish Pillbert loss and has just 22.2 in Philly colors, though Kai's record still trails Alan's by three games.
JMoney's early winner is cooling off: Likely scored 2.2, Boston 4.2, and Egbuka did not play. Likely still has 50 since the deal, but this week it gave Jordan almost nothing in a 37-point loss.

bios.1: Sonny's crew hung 146.72 on Randy, the top score of week 7, and the title odds rocketed from 11% to 28%. A seven-move wire overhaul brought in Lamar Jackson and C.J. Stroud. At 5-2, a trip to Team Pillbert decides second place.
bios.2: Randy has lost four straight and sits 3-4 with 23% playoff odds, with Derrick Henry stuck in single digits. A ten-transaction purge brought in Jaylin Noel, DeMario Douglas and the Bears D/ST. JMoney in week 8 is the best chance to stop the bleeding.
bios.3: JMoney is 1-6 with 0% playoff odds after a 60.88-point week that wasted Joe Burrow's league-best 28.88. J.K. Dobbins is the newest arrival for Ladd McConkey. A week 8 matchup with skidding Randy is a chance to play spoiler.
bios.4: Philly's five-game streak ended in a 1.74-point loss to the rookie, with Jalen Coker's 1.4 the sore spot. Still 5-2 with 93% playoff odds, though title odds fell from 26% to 17%. The Horse visits in week 8 for second place.
bios.5: Kai fell to 2-5 after a 26-point loss to Habib, with Tee Higgins' 23.8 stuck on the bench and Davante Adams out. Jeanty keeps producing, and Aaron Rodgers is the latest wire addition. Playoff odds sit at 14% heading into a date with the HULK.
bios.6: Habib has won two straight and climbed to fourth at 3-4, with title odds more than doubling to 14% and playoff odds at 67%. Drake Maye has been a waiver jackpot, and even a 35-point Pollard on the bench couldn't stop the win. Zoe is next.
bios.7: Brucie is 6-1, riding a three-game streak with 927.4 points for, the most in the league by a mile. Playoff odds are locked at 100%, but title odds slid from 50% to 36% as the Horse heats up. Kai's Dawgs come to town in week 8.
bios.8: Z² snapped Philly's streak as a 28% underdog and has now beaten both teams tied for second. She's 3-4 with 6% playoff odds and the second-lowest points total in the league, so every win has to be earned. Habibsters are up next in a must-win.
